title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the analysis of an extension of groups (eq. 243 on the previous page). In it, \mathfrak{G}^+/\mu_{\mathfrak{G}} is an extension of a group \mathfrak{G}_3 by a free abelian group M. The previous page relates M to \mathbb{Z}^3, presumably of rank 3. It sits inside the late 'Longue Marche' material on the modular / Teichmüller-type groups generated by elements \rho, \sigma. These are plausibly of orders 3 and 2, as for PSL_2(\mathbb{Z}) = \mathbb{Z}/2 * \mathbb{Z}/3; this is inferred, not certain.

Previous page. Over a base S, the extension of the constant group (\mathfrak{G}_3)_S by the vector group \underline{M} (with \underline{M}(S) = M \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}} \Gamma(S,\mathcal{O}_S)) is split. Its splittings form, naturally, a torsor under \underline{M}: two splittings are conjugate by a unique section of \underline{M}.

First statement on this page. The splittings of (243) over S are the same as the splittings of the abstract group extension 1 \to \underline{M}(S) \to E(S) \to \mathfrak{G}_3 \to 1. That extension is the pushout of the 'universal' extension \mathfrak{G}^+/\mu_{\mathfrak{G}} of \mathfrak{G}_3 by M along M \to M \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}} \Gamma(S,\mathcal{O}_S). In cohomological terms, the class in H^2(\mathfrak{G}_3, M) dies in H^2(\mathfrak{G}_3, M \otimes A). Splittings are then a torsor under the crossed homomorphisms Z^1(\mathfrak{G}_3, M \otimes A). The torsor being under M \otimes A acting by conjugation means (M \otimes A)^{\mathfrak{G}_3} = 0 and H^1(\mathfrak{G}_3, M \otimes A) = 0. This is what happens, for example, for a finite group with suitable orders invertible in A and no invariants.

Corollary. Specialise to S = Spec(\hat{\mathcal{E}}), a completed coefficient ring, with M^\wedge = M \otimes \hat{\mathcal{E}}. The completed extension \mathfrak{G}^{+\wedge}/\mu of \mathfrak{G}_3 by M^\wedge is split, and its splittings form an M^\wedge-torsor. The parenthetical, partly illegible, seems to say 'for infinitesimal [automorphisms/sections]'.

Second part: a lifting problem. Fix one splitting, written as
(257) \rho' = \xi\rho, \sigma' = \eta\sigma,
with \xi = a_0\lambda_0 + a_1\lambda_1 and \eta = b\delta = b(\lambda_1 - \lambda_0) in additive notation in M. Here \lambda_0, \lambda_1 are basis-type elements of M and \delta = \lambda_1 - \lambda_0. Grothendieck then asks for the liftings \mathcal{O}_{12}^* \to G_{\rho,\sigma}/\mu_G compatible with this splitting, i.e. commuting with \rho' and \sigma'. Here \mathcal{O}_{12}^* is a torus or unit group attached to level 12, presumably related to 12th roots of unity.

The next page carries this out by computing the centraliser of (\rho',\sigma'). Its image in (\mathfrak{G}_3)_{\rho_0} lies in the centre, hence is trivial, so the centraliser lies in \mathcal{O}_{12}^* \cdot \underline{M}. Writing elements as \lambda u_\mu, the commutation condition becomes a linear equation in M.

The purpose is to classify the 'rigidified' structures (splittings plus compatible tori) on the group G_{\rho,\sigma}. This is part of describing the automorphism and extension structure of the modular-type group scheme in the Longue Marche programme.
errors: No mathematical error is visible on this page. The argument is standard bookkeeping in group cohomology (pushout of an extension along M \to M \otimes A; torsor structure on splittings when H^1 = 0 and invariants vanish).
The legibility of key words is poor, and the transcription's equation number '(25)' is almost certainly '(257)', since the next page continues with (258).

ideas.what: Splittings of an extension of a constant group by a vector group \underline{M} over S correspond to splittings of the abstract extension obtained by pushing out the universal extension along M \to M \otimes \Gamma(S,\mathcal{O}_S); the splittings form an \underline{M}-torsor.
ideas.modern_name: Pushout of group extensions; torsor of splittings / H^1, H^2 of a group with coefficients
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Schreier, Eilenberg–MacLane; scheme version in SGA 3)
ideas.where_published: General formalism of extensions and torsors in SGA 3 / SGA 7; not this specific instance

ideas.what: Corollary that the completed extension \mathfrak{G}^{+\wedge}/\mu by M^\wedge is split, with splittings an M^\wedge-torsor.
ideas.modern_name: Splitting of an extension after base change to a completed coefficient ring

ideas.what: Setting up the classification of lifts of a torus \mathcal{O}_{12}^* into G_{\rho,\sigma}/\mu compatible with a chosen splitting (\rho' = \xi\rho, \sigma' = \eta\sigma), via computing a centraliser.
ideas.modern_name: Centraliser computation / rigidification of a group with generators of orders 2 and 3 (modular-group type) together with a torus action
ideas.usually_credited_to: No specific attribution; part of Grothendieck's unpublished Longue Marche analysis
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981, circulated) contains related material on the modular group and Teichmüller groupoids; this exact computation is uncertain

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine technical step: cohomological splitting of an extension and torsor of splittings, then setting up a centraliser computation. It is embedded in a larger unpublished analysis whose global objects (\mathfrak{G}_3, \mathcal{O}_{12}^*, G_{\rho,\sigma}) are only partially identifiable. Nothing here would by itself surprise a specialist.

'transitive[?] à un isomorphisme[?] de détermination[?]' is unreliable. The hand looks more like 'relatives à un ensemble de détermination' or similar; uncertain.
'(on dessine[?] a (\mathfrak{G}_3, \xi_0))' probably reads '(on désigne...)' with subscript \rho_0, i.e. '(\mathfrak{G}_3)_{\rho_0}', consistent with the next page.
'(pour [?] [?] infinitésimaux [?])' appears to end with '... infinitésimaux)'; the parenthesis qualifies the torsor statement.
